solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stepney's rough but not affected by mouse activity, last couple being sent west

indicators.note: west is leftward in an across entry, so the final pair of letters moves back towards the start of the word

parts.note: a button not pressed by a computer mouse has not been clicked

explanation.surface: Someone from East London feels poorly but has stayed clear of the mice in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Stepney is in London's East End, home of Cockney rhyming slang, where this phrase rhymes with sick. In an across entry west is leftward.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang uses the phrase for sick, and feeling rough is British for feeling unwell, so a Stepney speaker would say it.

clue.text: I'm hesitant to take mixed martial arts in religious community

indicators.note: one item taking another holds it inside, so the hesitant sound wraps round the next piece

parts.note: the noise a hesitant speaker makes
the usual abbreviation for the combat sport

explanation.surface: A hesitant speaker wonders about taking up cage fighting within a religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' looks like an anagram signal, but it is part of the sport's name, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ummah is the worldwide body of Muslim believers, a faith-based fellowship bound together by Islam.

clue.text: Curving semilune showing hysterical disposition?

indicators.note: something hysterical is wildly out of control, so the preceding letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the fifteen letters of these two words, all of them used

explanation.surface: A crescent-shaped line is read as a sign of an excitable temperament, as a palm reader might claim.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: palmists call this crescent line on the hand the girdle of Venus and say it reveals a nervous, emotional nature.
explanation.definitionFit: In palmistry this Latin-named half-moon line below the fingers is said to betray an oversensitive, highly-strung character.

clue.text: No longer make a subordinate see dope blocking road to the north

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading north means reading upwards, from the bottom to the top
something blocking a route sits in the middle of it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a lane is a minor road
v is short for Latin vide, see, used in references
a dope is a fool

explanation.surface: An instruction about drugs obstructing a northbound road, beside a hint about rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks the word as obsolete; 'see' is the reference abbreviation V.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic verb meaning to reduce to vassalage, turning a person into a feudal underling, so making a subordinate.

clue.text: Broke in to express pleasure over cutting crazy diet

indicators.note: over in a down clue tells you to turn the word upside down, so it reads upwards
something cutting into a word splits it and sits inside it
crazy means deranged, so the letters of the next word are disordered

parts.note: the four letters to be rearranged
a contented cat purrs

explanation.surface: Someone broke in to say how pleased they were to be cutting a mad diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diet' looks like the subject of the surface; it is only the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to burst or force your way inside suddenly, so the past tense matches forced entry.

clue.text: Veil of doom almost engulfing society

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
to engulf is to swallow up and surround, so the letters go round the next piece

parts.note: kismet is fate or doom, here missing its final letter
S is the standard abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A veil of doom nearly swallowing all of society: a gothic image.
explanation.walkthrough: KISMET loses its T; the S for society slips in after KIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists the name for a small, flirtatious bonnet or veil-trimmed hat, the sort that invites a peck on the cheek.

clue.text: Tolstoy's margins still illustrative of poetry

definitions.note: the word is the poetic form of typical; 'of poetry' labels its register

indicators.note: the margins of a page are its edges, so only the outermost letters of the name count

parts.note: the first and last letters of the novelist's name
a still is a photograph, a pic

explanation.surface: Tolstoy's handwritten margin notes are still examples of poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb meaning yet; it is a noun, a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for typical, meaning serving as a representative example, which is what illustrative means.

clue.text: NZ rail travel regularly covers kilometres — I get it

indicators.note: to cover something is to go around it, so these letters enclose the next ones
regularly means at even intervals, here every other letter starting with the first

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of the word
k is the abbreviation for kilometres
the exclamation of sudden understanding

explanation.surface: A New Zealand railway trip regularly runs to many kilometres, and the traveller finally understands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail' is not a train line but a bird family; NZ is New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: The takahe is a large flightless bird of New Zealand belonging to the rail family, Rallidae.

clue.text: Standard gene variant transmitted by duct primarily affects solid figures

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
an allele is one of the alternative forms of a gene
sent along a pipe

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the following word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A genetics paper: a common gene form spread through a duct mainly affects solid tissues.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural is the Latin-style -A ending.
explanation.definitionFit: A parallelepiped is a three-dimensional shape with six parallelogram faces, so the plural names a group of such solid figures.

clue.text: Free advisory organisation admits endless confusion with note brought up for cancer drug

indicators.note: endless means without its final letter, which is dropped
to admit is to let in, so the organisation holds the other letters inside

parts.note: the Citizens Advice Bureau gives free advice in Britain

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing letters up means reading them from the bottom

parts.note: a mix-up is confusion, here missing its last letter
the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A free advice service admits its confusion about a musical note raised over a cancer drug.
explanation.walkthrough: The Citizens Advice Bureau is a British charity offering free help. The confusion and the note are reversed together before going inside, after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cetuximab is a monoclonal antibody medicine used to treat bowel and head and neck tumours.

clue.text: What helps make ermine vermin? Its fur

indicators.note: something that only helps make a thing is a part of it, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A riddle about what turns the noble ermine into lowly vermin.
explanation.walkthrough: The riddle invites letter-swapping between the two near-anagrams, but the fur is simply sitting across the join. 'Its' points back to the ermine.
explanation.definitionFit: Miniver is the white fur, often from stoats in winter coat, used to trim ceremonial robes, so it is the ermine's pelt.

clue.text: Wheeling Russian sandpiper like a big old falcon

indicators.note: wheeling means turning round, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the Terek sandpiper is named after a Russian river
as means like

explanation.surface: A Russian wading bird circles, looking like a large falcon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The sakeret is the male of the saker, a large hunting falcon, an archaic falconry term.

clue.text: Worms' dwelling with 500 in Glaswegian's clutches

indicators.note: in says the number is placed inside the dwelling

parts.note: Worms is a German city, and the German for house is Haus
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A wormery holding 500 creatures in a Scotsman's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worms' looks like the garden creatures; it is the city on the Rhine, so its dwelling is German.
explanation.definitionFit: Haud is Scots for hold, so the verb form matches clutches, as a Glasgow speaker would say it.

clue.text: Display sacred cross that may cause itchy palms

parts.note: pomp is grand display
a direct synonym
an X is a cross

explanation.surface: Showing off a holy crucifix could make someone's hands itch, perhaps for money.
explanation.walkthrough: Itchy palms usually suggests greed; here it is the literal skin complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompholyx is a form of eczema producing intensely itchy blisters on the hands and feet.

clue.text: I lie in excessively idle talk, getting twisted awkwardly around

indicators.note: around says the twisting word wraps itself about the talk

parts.note: to slue is to swing or twist round clumsily
gab is chatter

explanation.surface: A confession: too much time in bed and too much chatter leave one tangled up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the answer itself: 'I lie in excessively' describes the person.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy person who stays under the covers late in the morning is called a slugabed.

clue.text: Fresh bun and loaves worth relating to cost

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are given a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bakery boast: freshly baked rolls and bread are worth the price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is the link; the fodder is the two bakery words.
explanation.definitionFit: Snob value is the appeal a product gains from being expensive or exclusive, desirability tied to price.

clue.text: Perhaps a summer of heartless pandemonium

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letters are taken out

parts.note: bedlam is uproar

explanation.surface: A summer of cruel chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer' looks like the season; it is a builder's term for a main beam, so 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A summer is a large horizontal timber supporting floor joists, one kind of structural beam.

clue.text: Liberace emptied gold into thickening stacks of money

indicators.note: into says these letters are put inside the next word

parts.note: a roux of fat and flour thickens sauces
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: emptying removes the contents, leaving just the first and last letters

parts.note: the pianist's name without its middle

explanation.surface: The flamboyant pianist Liberace pours his gold into growing piles of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thickening' looks like an adjective for the stacks but is the cookery noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A rouleau is a cylindrical paper-wrapped column of coins, so the plural means piles of cash.

clue.text: Russian recipient of prize for physics, forced over neck

definitions.text: Russian recipient of prize for physics

indicators.note: forced means wrenched out of shape, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: the two words, all eight letters

explanation.surface: A Russian Nobel physicist was made to bend over by the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: Pavel Cherenkov, also spelt Cerenkov, shared the 1958 Nobel award in physics for discovering the radiation named after him.

clue.text: It's plain Mary stuffing mouth

indicators.note: stuffing goes inside, so these letters are packed into the next word

parts.note: os is Latin for mouth, used in anatomy
BV is short for Blessed Virgin, the Virgin Mary

explanation.surface: Clearly Mary is stuffing her face.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary is the Blessed Virgin, and the mouth is the Latin anatomical word.
explanation.definitionFit: Obvs is informal clipped slang for obviously, said when something is clear and needs no argument.

clue.text: Elizabethan fragrant plant eater's absorbing English book

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the letter goes inside the eater

parts.note: to nosh is to eat
the standard abbreviation
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A sweet-smelling Tudor herb, and someone eating an English book.
explanation.walkthrough: Nosh is British slang for food, so a nosher is someone eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare used the term for a scented plant in a nosegay, grown for its smell rather than as food.

clue.text: Internal organs ultimately destroy neighbour of Kildare

parts.note: offal is the edible innards of an animal

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of the word is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Destroying internal organs suggests a grisly scene, with an Irish county tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: Offaly is an Irish county in the Midlands sharing a border with County Kildare to its east.

clue.text: Dance scene goes on to create a shrill cry in WI

definitions.text: create a shrill cry in WI
definitions.note: a regional word; WI is the West Indies

parts.note: sc. is the abbreviation for scene in a play
a reel is a lively folk dance

explanation.surface: A dance scene carries on into someone shrieking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes on' says the dance follows the scene. WI is the West Indies, where the word is used, as in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To screel is to scream or screech, a dialect verb for letting out a high piercing yell.

clue.text: Five clean up the spout with poisonous effect

indicators.note: up the spout is British slang for ruined, so the letters are wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters of both words

explanation.surface: Five people clean a drainpipe spout, with toxic results.
explanation.definitionFit: Venefical is an archaic adjective from Latin veneficus, meaning acting by poison or sorcery, so toxic in effect.

clue.text: Climax of haj in Muslim festival over communal farm

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the festival

parts.note: Eid is a Muslim festival

indicators.note: the climax is the end, so only the last letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the final letter of the pilgrimage
o is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: The high point of the pilgrimage to Mecca falls during a Muslim festival on a shared farm.
explanation.definitionFit: An ejido is a Mexican cooperative landholding farmed jointly by a village community.

clue.text: East German and eastern Australian in less familiar guise

parts.note: Ossi is German slang for a former East German
the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: An East German and an Australian from the east coast are both in disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less familiar guise' says this is a rare spelling of the usual informal word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossie is an uncommon variant spelling of Aussie, the informal word for a native of Australia.

clue.text: Lazy, outdated British leaving to smear European

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: the standard abbreviation
to blur is to smudge
a Dane is a European from Denmark

explanation.surface: A sluggish British has-been leaves to slander someone from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outdated' is part of the definition, marking the word as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurdane is an archaic adjective and noun for sluggish or idle, a dull good-for-nothing.

clue.text: Smaller seabirds allowed to stop large one returning

indicators.note: something stopping a gap plugs it, so these letters go inside
returning means going back, so the bird's name reads from right to left

parts.note: the skua is a large predatory seabird
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Little seabirds are permitted to block a big one flying back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large one' must be read as a big seabird, prompted by the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Auklets are small members of the auk family of diving birds found in the North Pacific.

clue.text: Will's put in vault, trying to lose page containing name

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the next letter goes within
to lose means to drop, so the page letter is cut away

parts.note: pesky means annoying, trying
the standard abbreviation
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A last will is locked in a vault after a page is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will's' is Shakespeare's usage, and the vault is the vault of heaven, not a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare used the verb to mean place in heaven, as if lifting someone up into the sky's arch.

clue.text: Long Island team quickly accepts lead for Archibald Leach

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so that letter goes inside

parts.note: the usual abbreviation
a team of eleven, written in Roman numerals
vite is the musical direction for fast

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: A Long Island team quickly signs Archibald Leach, the real name of Cary Grant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Archibald Leach' reads as one famous name, but it splits: 'Leach' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To lixiviate is to extract a soluble substance by washing it through with water, which is what leaching does.
